content:
New of Robert Pattinson’s James Bond casting made its way from water cooler chats and “Twilight” message boards all the way to the British royal family’s Twitter account.

King Charles weighed in on the casting choice that came out of left field on Monday, as earlier reports suggested that Bond might be played by Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor or Nicholas Hoult.

“Welcome to His Majesty’s Secret Service, Mr. Bond,” the royal family’s tweet said, reposting an announcement showing Pattinson as the famous spy.

Given the late Queen Elizabeth’s 70-year reign, this is the first time in the film franchise that a Bond will serve under a British king.

Queen Elizabeth famously made an appearance alongside Daniel Craig ― in character as Bond ― at the opening ceremony of the 2012 London Olympics.

In a now-iconic sketch, Craig heads to Buckingham Palace to pick up the queen and fly to the opening ceremony together in a helicopter.

Stunt doubles dressed as the two then parachuted out of the helicopter while the Bond theme song played, and the queen then took her seat at the stadium.

The skit was a hit, leaving one Olympic announcer to say at the time, “Never has Her Majesty been introduced to her public like that.”

Elizabeth even has a line in the skit ― “Good evening, Mr. Bond” ― which wasn’t planned.

Author Frank Cottrell-Boyce, who wrote the scene, revealed that the queen “wanted to be in the sketch.”

“On the day we were filming, she said to [director] Danny Boyle, ‘I think I should have a line,’” he said in an interview with BBC in 2022. “She bagged that. She didn’t have a line in the script.”

Queen Elizabeth’s close friend and dresser, Angela Kelly, revealed more behind-the-scenes information about the sketch in her 2019 book, “The Other Side of the Coin: The Queen, the Dresser and the Wardrobe.”

“I asked then if she would like a speaking part,” Kelly wrote. “Without hesitation, Her Majesty replied: ‘Of course I must say something. After all, he is coming to rescue me.’”

“I asked whether she would like to say: ‘Good evening, James,’ or: ‘Good evening, Mr. Bond,’ and she chose the latter, knowing the Bond films,” Kelly said, adding that she then delivered “the good news to Danny [Boyle]— I think he almost fell off his chair when I said that the Queen’s only stipulation was that she could deliver that iconic line.”
